## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned images, validation manifest

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format — the shared contract between the
Dashboard's tutorial gallery (which launches tutorials) and the curated
tutorial content (which is packaged and tested per the format). The format
specifies the metadata a tutorial carries, how tutorials pin the images they
run on, and the validation manifest used to test them, so that tutorials are
versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- Specify the metadata a packaged tutorial carries (identity, journey,
  description, version).
- Specify how a tutorial pins the workbench image it runs on.
- Specify the validation manifest for a packaged tutorial, and how executing
  it produces a pass/fail validation result without requiring a Dashboard
  release.
- Specify versioning rules so a tutorial's version is independent of the
  Dashboard release version.
- Carry the format to acceptance with the consuming parties: the Dashboard
  team (gallery launch mechanics) and the tutorial content owners.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification defines the tutorial metadata, pinned
  image references, and validation manifest such that a tutorial can be
  packaged from the specification alone.
- A tutorial packaged per the format is versioned independently of the
  Dashboard release version.
- Executing a packaged tutorial's validation manifest produces a pass/fail
  result without requiring a Dashboard release.
- The format is reviewed and accepted by the Dashboard team and the tutorial
  content owners.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): tutorial packaging format defined so tutorials are versioned
  and testable independently of Dashboard releases. This epic's priority is
  P0 by inheritance: the format transitively enables the P0 gallery and P0
  curated-tutorial requirements, and an epic blocking all P0 work is
  implicitly P0.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch

## Description

Adds a tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a browsable set of maintained,
tested tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with one
click — opening a workbench containing the tutorial notebook, or importing
the tutorial pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance.

## Scope

- Gallery surface in the Dashboard listing available tutorials with the
  metadata defined by the tutorial packaging format.
- Launch mechanics for notebook tutorials: launch into the user's project by
  opening a workbench containing the tutorial notebook, running the image
  pinned in the tutorial's packaging.
- Launch mechanics for pipeline tutorials: launch into the user's project by
  importing the pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance.
- Development-time verification of launches using a tutorial conforming to
  the packaging format (fixture), so the gallery can be built and validated
  before the curated tutorial set is complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can browse the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and launch a
  tutorial into their own project with one click.
- Launching a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project that
  contains the tutorial notebook, running the image pinned in the tutorial's
  packaging.
- Launching a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline into the user's project.
- A tutorial that conforms to the tutorial packaging format is launchable
  from the gallery without Dashboard code changes — the gallery consumes the
  packaging format rather than hard-coding tutorials.
- The Dashboard build pipeline is green with the gallery changes merged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline).

# Six curated tutorials covering the core journeys

## Description

Authors the six curated tutorials covering the core platform journeys —
first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first
deployment, first RAG app — each packaged per the tutorial packaging format
(metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) and tested against the
current release. This is content authoring: the deliverable is maintained,
tested tutorial content, not platform code.

## Scope

- Author six tutorials covering the core journeys: first workbench, data
  prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  images, and a validation manifest, with a version independent of Dashboard
  releases.
- Validate each tutorial against the current release: the notebook tutorials
  complete in a workbench on the current release; the pipeline tutorial
  imports and runs through Data Science Pipelines on the current release.
- Keep the tutorials in a maintained location from which validation can be
  re-run for each release.
- Component span: the primary medium is notebooks running in workbenches
  (Notebooks component); the first-pipeline tutorial targets Data Science
  Pipelines. Both components are passive in this strategy — no code changes
  to either; their continued functioning is verified by the tutorial
  validation above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Six tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data
  prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest) and carries a version independent of
  Dashboard releases.
- Each tutorial's validation manifest passes against the current release:
  notebook tutorials complete in a workbench on the current release, and the
  pipeline tutorial imports and runs via Data Science Pipelines on the
  current release.
- The tutorials reside in a maintained location from which their validation
  manifests can be re-executed for a future release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): six curated tutorials covering the core journeys, each tested
  against the current release.

## Risks / Notes

- Notebooks and Data Science Pipelines are passive (no code changes
  expected). If tutorial validation exposes gaps in either component on the
  current release, additional component work outside this decomposition
  would be required.

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for users and contributors: how to use the
gallery to launch tutorials into a project, and how to contribute new
tutorials through the packaging format and validation process. Produced via
the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Using the gallery: browsing the tutorial gallery and launching tutorials
  into a project — opening a workbench with a tutorial notebook, and
  importing a tutorial pipeline.
- Contributing new tutorials: the packaging format requirements (metadata,
  pinned images, validation manifest), how validation is run against a
  release, and the review path for new tutorials. The contribution process
  is documented only — no submission tooling is in scope this release, and
  the documentation must not promise any.
- Localization of tutorial content is out of scope; the documentation is
  authored in English only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery: browsing
  tutorials and launching them into a project (workbench notebooks and
  pipeline imports).
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials:
  packaging format requirements, validation, and the review path — and does
  not describe submission tooling (out of scope this release).
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery,
  the curated tutorial set, and the tutorial packaging format.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials. Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring
  priority exception (strategy priority Major → P1).

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

## Triage Outcome

Not below-threshold and not docs-only. The strategy explicitly spans three
architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review
processes — product code (the gallery and launch mechanics), substantive
content authoring (the tutorials themselves), and documentation — across four
affected components (Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines,
Documentation). The multiple-distinct-work-streams escape condition applies,
so the strategy receives a full multi-epic decomposition.

## Step 1 — Strategy Structure

- **High Level Requirements**: HLR-1 (P0, gallery + one-click launch),
  HLR-2 (P0, six curated tested tutorials), HLR-3 (P1, tutorial packaging
  format), HLR-4 (P2, gallery + contribution documentation).
- **Affected Components**: Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines,
  Documentation (listed as bullets — no change descriptions or owner teams).
- **Open Questions**: none. No conditional ADRs, pending reviews, or risks
  table → no Investigation epics.

## Step 2 — Component Graph

All four affected components are canonical RHAI Jira components
(`.context/rhai-components.txt`); no invented names were needed.

- **Dashboard** — active (new gallery UI + launch mechanics). Owner: RHOAI

- **Notebooks** — passive: no notebook-controller or workbench code changes;
  tutorials run in existing workbenches against pinned workbench images.
  Validation becomes acceptance criteria on the tutorial content epic.
- **Data Science Pipelines** — passive: no DSP code changes; the pipeline

- The curated tutorial content epic is assigned to **Notebooks** (owner:
